one_line: Early Western Ganga king and learned patron of Sanskrit, Jain and emerging Kannada traditions, ruling Gangavadi in the 6th century CE.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but athletic build, medium height with a poised, disciplined stance.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp jawline, warm medium-brown South Indian complexion, straight nose, slightly arched brows, calm large anime-style eyes with a thoughtful gaze, and a composed, gentle half-smile suggesting introspective confidence.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and neatly tied into a high, tight topknot at the back of the crown, front hair smoothed back with no loose strands; a simple gold circlet-diadem resting low on the forehead, decorated at the center with a small engraved lotus motif.
appearance.costume: He wears a finely draped off-white cotton dhoti wrapped snugly around the waist and extending to the ankles with a slightly flared hem, bordered with a narrow maroon stripe; over the torso a fitted, short-sleeved, light-cream cotton angiya (upper garment) that covers the chest and is secured neatly, and across his left shoulder and chest a rich deep-green silk uttariya shawl with subtle gold thread edging, flowing down his back and over one forearm; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is modest but royal—two thin gold armlets on each upper arm, a single layered gold necklace with small round beads, and gold studs in the ears; the overall tailoring and drape evoke a 6th-century Deccan royal but are restrained, emphasizing scholarly dignity more than opulence.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle bound with a red cord held in his left hand, with a narrow bronze stylus tucked at the top, while his right hand lightly touches the hilt of a short, straight-edged iron sword in a plain brown scabbard at his waist, symbolizing both learning and kingship.

ref_desc: Durvinita appears as a mid-30s, lean brown-skinned king with an oval face, black topknot, gold circlet, off-white dhoti, cream angiya, deep-green silk shawl, modest gold jewellery, palm-leaf manuscript with stylus, and a plain-hilted sword in off-white, deep green, maroon, gold and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model of Durvinita of the Western Ganga: a mid-30s lean South Indian king with an oval face, warm brown complexion, calm large eyes and a composed half-smile, thick black hair oiled into a high tight topknot and a simple gold circlet-diadem with a small lotus at the center. He wears a finely wrapped off-white dhoti to the ankles with a narrow maroon border, a modest light-cream short-sleeved angiya covering his torso, and a deep-green silk uttariya shawl edged in subtle gold draped from his left shoulder across his chest and flowing behind him. Show simple brown leather sandals and restrained royal jewellery—thin gold armlets, a single layered gold bead necklace and small gold ear studs. In his left hand he firmly holds a palm-leaf manuscript bundle bound with a red cord, with a slender bronze stylus visible at the top, while his right hand lightly rests on the hilt of a short straight-edged iron sword in a plain brown scabbard at his waist, balancing scholar and warrior. Use a palette dominated by off-white, deep green, maroon, gold and brown, and present him front-facing with clear visibility of face, hair, costume details and signature manuscript-sword combination.
